answer: Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Reaching the walnut of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. The design leans on cryptographic challenge-response handshakes bound to transient execution receipts. Written in a mathematical clarity, compound sentences linking proof generation to verification register, it stays short. The cipher holds work receipts rather than names, so the ivory of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
